name: Ireland

meta.title: Study in Ireland from India: fees, living costs, stay-back
meta.description: Irish tuition fee ranges by subject in rupees, the €10,000 living cost rule, the September intake, the Stamp 1G stay-back and the Government of Ireland scholarship.

summary: Clear fee ranges by subject, a fixed €10,000 living cost rule, and up to 2 years of stay-back after a master's.

whyReasons.text: Master's graduates (level 9) can stay for up to 24 months to look for work under the Third Level Graduate Programme. Honours bachelor's graduates (level 8) get up to 12 months.
The living cost rule is simple: show €10,000 for each year of study, plus fees.
The Government of Ireland scholarship gives a full fee waiver for one year and a €10,000 stipend, and students from India can apply.

ug.note: 2025/26 non-EU fees for business, engineering, science and arts. Medicine and health sciences cost €50,135 to €62,500.

pg.note: 2025/26 non-EU fees. Business courses run up to €40,000, engineering up to €30,000.

living.note: This is the minimum Irish immigration asks you to show for each academic year. Dublin rents are high, so budget more if you study there.

visaFunds.text: Show immediate access to at least €10,000 for the first year of living costs, and €10,000 for each later year, in addition to course fees.

intakes.note: Most Irish universities start their academic year in September.

afterStudy.text: Third Level Graduate Programme (Stamp 1G): up to 12 months for a level 8 honours bachelor's, up to 24 months for a level 9 master's or higher (granted as 12 months, then renewed for 12 more).

pr.text: With a Critical Skills Employment Permit, you can apply for long-term residence after 60 months of residence permission. Graduates who got their degree in the last 12 months qualify for this permit at a lower salary threshold of €36,848 in listed occupations.

scholarships.name: Government of Ireland International Education Scholarships
scholarships.text: Full fee waiver for one year plus a €10,000 stipend. The call usually closes in March for a September start.

faq.q: How much money do I need to show for Ireland?
faq.a: At least €10,000 for each year of living costs, in addition to your course fees.

faq.q: How long can I stay in Ireland after a master's?
faq.a: Up to 24 months under the Third Level Graduate Programme. You get 12 months first, then a 12-month renewal if you are actively looking for graduate work.

faq.q: What does a master's in Ireland cost?
faq.a: For 2025/26, non-EU postgraduate fees range from about €11,000 to €40,000 a year depending on the subject. Business courses are at the top of that range.
Most Irish universities start in September.
